rules.universe: Active (pending) DEALS rows with a US, UK or European target. Excludes at-risk, hostile, contested-without-agreement and rumored deals.
qualityScreen: Signed definitive agreement (or recommended UK/Irish scheme or offer)
Financing committed (no financing condition, or UK/Irish Code cash confirmation)
Limited antitrust/regulatory risk: no second request, CMA Phase 2 / EU Phase 2, sector-regulator veto risk, or contested high-threshold tender condition
Target board recommendation and/or shareholder support
Sensible return: annualized spread of at least ~3% (at least ~5% for the daily add screen), unless closing is imminent
Break protection: termination fees from the merger agreement are scored; a large reverse (acquirer-paid, incl. regulatory) fee is preferred because it compensates holders if the deal breaks
rules.sizing: Downside-based sizing (from Nov 10, 2026): size by potential loss, not expected gain. New positions are sized so a break costs about 1.75% of NAV: weight = 1.75% / downside, clamped to 3%-10%. Downside = (current price - break price) / current price, with the break price estimated as the undisturbed close before announcement (Yahoo history), or a default 25% downside when that price is unavailable or the deal leaked early. Positions whose break loss exceeds 3% of NAV are trimmed back to the downside-based size. Inception positions were bought at an equal 7%.
rules.hedging: Stock and cash+stock deals with a fixed exchange ratio: short the acquirer at the ratio on entry (proceeds credited to cash). Fixed-dollar or NAV-based stock legs are not share-hedged.
rules.pricing: Entries and daily marks use closing prices from the site's live quote feed (Yahoo-backed) in each listing's local currency; returns are measured in local currency (FX assumed hedged).
rules.closings: When a deal completes it is booked at deal value (cash plus ratio x acquirer close); the hedge is covered with the acquirer shares received.
rules.breaks: When a deal is terminated it is sold at that day's close and the loss is booked; the hedge is covered at the acquirer close.
rules.rebalancing: No rebalancing of open positions. Cash from closings and breaks is redeployed into new names that pass the screen, at 7% each, only while cash stays at or above 5% of NAV after the purchase.
rules.nav: NAV = cash + long market value - short market value, recorded once per trading day after the US close (stamped with the session date).
rules.qualityScore: Each deal gets a 0-100 quality score: closing probability (40 pts), annualized spread capped at 15% (25), reverse termination fee as % of equity value, full credit at 6%+ (20), deal risk low/medium/high (10/5/0), target break fee, full credit at 4%+ (5; UK Takeover Code deals, where target break fees are not permitted, get a neutral 2.5). Fees come from the merger agreement, 8-K or Rule 2.7 announcement and are shown on the holdings table as reverse / break fee %. Larger fees are better: a big reverse or regulatory fee is paid to the target if the buyer walks or regulators block the deal, which cushions a break.
rules.swaps: A holding is swapped for a candidate only when the candidate passes the quality screen and the quant pre-screen, was not excluded for a qualitative reason, and its quality score beats the weakest holding's by at least 15 points. Swaps trade at the session close and are logged.
rules.feeReview: Nov 5, 2026 re-rank after adding termination fees: weakest holdings are PTC (score 50.9; its merger agreement has no reverse fee, so a break in the long Q3 2027 review would be uncompensated) and SLN (52.2; ~3% annualized, no reverse fee). Top fee-protected candidates LXFR (~7% reverse fee) and CHMI (~6.8%) score higher on the site's stored spreads, but at the Nov 5 close their live spreads were only ~0.4% (LXFR, ~2.6% annualized) and ~0.7% (CHMI, ~4.8%), below the return screen, so no swap was made. PTC and SLN are flagged; they will be swapped if a candidate clears the screen on live prices with a 15+ point score lead.
rules.diversification: Many small positions and no single deal above 10% of NAV; at most 25% of NAV in one industry or awaiting the same regulator. Cash is not forced into thin spreads: unallocated capital stays in cash when no candidate clears the screen on live prices.
principles: Hedge stock deals: buy the target and short the acquirer at the exchange ratio, so the position earns the spread rather than taking market direction.
Underwrite the downside: estimate a break price (the undisturbed pre-announcement close) and the paths by which the deal could fail before sizing.
Size by potential loss, not expected gain: about 1.75% of NAV lost per deal break, weights 3%-10%, trim when break loss exceeds 3% of NAV.
Diversify: many small positions, at most ~10% of NAV per deal and 25% per industry or awaiting the same regulator.
Low leverage: gross exposure stays modest; returns should come from spreads, not borrowing.
Don't force capital into thin spreads: cash stays in cash when nothing clears the screen on live prices.
Bottom-up research: each deal is underwritten from its merger agreement, filings and regulatory path; complex deals with real research edge are preferred to crowded 'safe' spreads.

Reported competing bid; terms may change
Highly levered buyer; outside date late 2027
e.g. ITGR, MKTX, PCRX, TECH, BOW: annualized return below ~3% with no imminent close

positions.acquirer: Ares Capital Corporation (Nasdaq: ARCC), with cash contribution from a subsidiary of Ares Management (NYSE: ARES)
positions.rationale: Ares Capital (largest US BDC) buying MFIC for $10.88/share ($1.21 cash + $9.67 of ARCC stock, priced at the greater of ARCC NAV or market). Strategic, well-capitalised buyer; both boards unanimous, Apollo affiliates support; no antitrust overlap. The stock leg is a fixed dollar amount converted at closing, so there is no static share hedge.

deal.dealTerms: Definitive merger agreement announced October 27, 2026. MFIC stockholders receive total consideration of $10.88 per fully diluted share, consisting of ~$1.21 in cash and ~$9.67 in Ares Capital common stock (reduced dollar-for-dollar for a pre-closing MFIC special dividend of undistributed taxable income). Exchange ratio uses ARCC value equal to the greater of NAV per share and share price; MFIC holders share 50% of any ARCC premium to NAV up to 104.5% of NAV. 30.1% premium to MFIC's October 26, 2026 close and 25.8% premium to 30-day VWAP; preliminary Sept 30 NAV ~$12.86. Unanimously approved by both boards on the MFIC special committee's recommendation. Apollo affiliates holding 5.2% signed voting and support agreements. Conditions: MFIC stockholder approval, regulatory approvals, customary conditions. Expected to close in the first half of 2027. Pro forma ownership ~95% ARCC / ~5% MFIC
deal.description: Ares Capital, the largest publicly traded BDC, is acquiring Apollo-managed MidCap Financial Investment Corporation in a stock-and-cash deal with a total enterprise value of about $2.6bn. The transaction adds a portfolio of senior secured middle-market loans and more than 200 incumbent positions, taking ARCC's pro forma portfolio above $31bn at fair value. Ares expects the deal to be modestly accretive to core EPS.
deal.statusNote: Stock leg is a $9.67 dollar value converted at closing using ARCC price vs NAV (up to 1.0225x if ARCC trades above 104.5% of NAV), less any post-signing special tax dividend (paid separately in cash). $10.88 headline used (conservative).

Schneider Electric expects approximately €250 million of annual run-rate cost synergies by Year 3 and approximately €800 million of expected revenue synergies. Unanimously approved by both boards. Completion expected by Q3 2027, subject to PTC sh
deal.description: Schneider Electric has agreed to acquire PTC at $205.00 per share in cash, ~$22.6bn equity value / ~$23.7bn EV, a 42.3% premium to the 3 October close. Largest acquisition in Schneider Electric's history; thesis is combining PTC's CAD/PLM/IIoT stack with Schneider's industrial automation footprint to build an industrial-AI platform. 21x EV/Adj. EBITA 2027E standalone, 13x including run-rate synergies (€250m cost + ~€800m revenue). Targeted Q3 2027 close subject to PTC vote and multi-jurisdiction antitrust/FDI review.
deal.latestNote: (2026-10-05) New row. Schneider Electric announced the largest deal in its history: $205 cash per PTC share, ~$22.6bn equity / ~$23.7bn EV, a 42.3% premium to the 3 October close. Three things worth isolating. First, this is a plain all-cash spread with no financing condition disclosed - the arbitrage is sized by probability × time rather than by stock-leg volatility. Second, the multi-jurisdiction review is the real gate: US antitrust (software, moderate overlap), EU antitrust and FDI (Schneider is French with a strategic industrial asset moving across the Atlantic), and PTC's own shareholder vote. The parties guided to Q3 2027 completion, implying an ~11 month timetable which is realistic
deal.otherBidders: No competing proposal publicly disclosed as at the date of this entry.

deal.dealTerms: Definitive agreement announced October 29, 2026. ADT stockholders receive $10.00 per share in cash, a 45.6% premium to the unaffected closing price of $6.87 on October 27, 2026. Debt financing is committed solely by funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management; no financing condition. 30-day go-shop period expiring 11:59 p.m. New York time on November 28, 2026, with a possible 10-day extension for qualifying bidders. Conditions: ADT stockholder approval, expiration of the HSR waiting period and customary closing conditions. Expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, after which ADT will be delisted from the NYSE.
deal.description: Thrive Holdings is taking home-security provider ADT private for $10.00 per share in cash, valuing the company at about $15.3bn including debt, with Apollo (ADT's former controlling owner) providing the financing. ADT will become the foundation of Thrive's AI-enabled smart-home security business. The deal carries a go-shop through late November and is expected to close in Q1 2027 pending stockholder and antitrust approvals.
deal.latestNote: (2026-11-02) New row. Clean all-cash take-private with committed Apollo financing and only HSR plus a stockholder vote as gates; ADT traded just under the $10.00 offer after the announcement, indicating the market does not expect a topping bid during the go-shop (ends November 28, 2026). Verification: ADT Form 8-K (Exhibit 99.1) and DEFA14A of October 29, 2026; Bloomberg coverage of October 29, 2026; Axios Pro and TIKR coverage.
deal.otherBidders: None disclosed; go-shop runs to November 28, 2026.

deal.dealTerms: Definitive agreement announced October 19, 2026. Merck KGaA acquires Silence Therapeutics for $20.00 per American Depositary Share in cash (each ADS = three ordinary shares), an 82% premium to the 30-day VWAP of $10.99 and ~130% to the October 16 closing ADS price. Implemented via a UK scheme of arrangement. Unanimously approved by the Silence board; holders of ~14% of voting power signed voting and support agreements. Conditions: Silence shareholder approval and required regulatory approvals. Funded with new debt. Expected to close in Q1 2027.
deal.description: Merck KGaA is acquiring London-based Silence Therapeutics for $20 per ADS in cash (~$1.3bn equity value) to add divesiran, a Phase 3-ready siRNA therapy for polycythemia vera that met its Phase 2 primary endpoint (88% responder rate vs 19% placebo). The deal is Merck's first major acquisition under CEO Kai Beckmann and follows its 2025 SpringWorks purchase. UK scheme of arrangement; closing expected Q1 2027.
deal.statusNote: Spread on the Nasdaq ADS line.
deal.latestNote: (2026-10-21) New row. Clean strategic biotech takeout: cash, debt-funded by an investment-grade buyer, a scheme structure that needs 75% by value of votes cast, and no overlapping products to trigger antitrust concern. Main gating item is simply the UK court timetable. The 82% premium to VWAP after a competitive process leaves little room for a topping bid. Verification: Merck KGaA press release (issuer), Silence Therapeutics Form DEFA14A (SEC), BioPharma Dive and Fierce Biotech.
deal.otherBidders: Silence says the agreement followed a competitive sale process; no rival offer disclosed

target.note: Payable by Silence on superior proposal, change of recommendation, or tail; fee permitted under Transaction Agreement (scheme of arrangement)
